speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) in the past two years, how many incidences of unauthorised drones have occurred; (b) whether the offenders were found and, if so, what consequences did they face; and (c) whether there are plans to enforce a larger no-fly zone around major transport nodes, such as the airports.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether he can provide an update on the investigation of the recent incidents of flight delays at Changi Airport due to the presence of illegal drones and what further measures will be taken to prevent such incidents in the future.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Transport what are the measures put in place to ensure the prompt removal of drones that have intruded into restricted areas and their identification.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry has ascertained the persons responsible for the flying of the unauthorised drones which resulted in flight delays and the shutting of a runway at Changi Airport on 18 June 2019 and what are the actions to be taken to prevent similar delays in the future.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport with regard to the disruptions to flight operations at Changi Airport arising from unauthorised drones on 18, 19 and 24 June 2019 (a) whether the Government has identified the drones in question, the identity of their owners or operators and the reasons for their operation at the material time; and (b) what are the Government's plans to prevent or minimise further disruptions to airport operations from drone operations, especially by unregistered or unidentified owners or operators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the latest incident involving unauthorised drones adversely affecting the operation of Changi Airport (a) whether the Ministry has completed its investigation into the incident; and (b) what are the measures taken to prevent future incidents.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport how many drones have been detected in the recent two incidents involving unauthorised drones near Changi Airport and what is the outcome of the investigation thus far.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Although the impact of the recent drone intrusions has been moderate, these intrusions can have severe impact on airport operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At Gatwick Airport, for example, drone intrusions shut down the entire airport for three days, affecting approximately 1,000 flights.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Police investigations into the drone intrusions are ongoing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have learnt from the experiences of other airports that identifying the perpetrators can be challenging and will take time.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Meanwhile, our priority is to detect the drones promptly and prevent them from affecting air traffic and endangering public safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have taken a multi-agency approach and deployed national resources towards ensuring the safety of Changi Airport operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The drone intrusions have caused some to suggest that we should ban the use of drones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Besides commercial applications, such as drone deliveries and inspections, there are also many recreational users in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Our schools and institutes of higher learning use drones to teach Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics (STEM), including robotics and programming.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is, therefore, important that we continue to take a balanced approach.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: By and large, the community of drone enthusiasts fly their drones responsibly and are sensitive to the needs and concerns of other users that they share public space with in our crowded urban environment.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Our laws governing the use of drones prohibit their use within five kilometres (km) of an aerodrome, unless a permit has been granted by the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS).

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have assessed this no-fly zone prohibition to be sufficient.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, there will be a few selfish and irresponsible persons who operate in flagrant disregard of the law as well as the needs and concerns of others.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will, therefore, tighten the approach to regulating drone uses and dealing with errant drone users through the following measures.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will ensure that drone operators are made aware of their responsibilities and undertake to conduct their activities in a responsible manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Second, there will be stricter enforcement actions against errant drone operators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This morning, a company pleaded guilty to a charge of operating a drone without a permit.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Further, there is one other case being investigated for breaching the existing drone regulations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In conjunction with this, the Government is also looking into increasing the penalties for errant drone users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As with other forms of new technology, finding the right balance in terms of regulations will take time, particularly since drone technology continues to evolve very quickly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is why CAAS established the Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Advisory Panel earlier this year to help review and recommend enhancements to the regulatory framework.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Meanwhile, we have strengthened our counter-drone capabilities at the airport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We stand ready to invest in and deploy additional capabilities to monitor and enforce the safety of our airspace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am glad to hear that the Ministry is looking into compulsory registration of drones.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that this could be done sooner rather than later.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, can the Senior Minister of State provide an estimated timeline when drone registration may take place?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second question is we need to go beyond registration.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We know that some of this technology allows the operator to fly the drones beyond a certain distance.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Given Singapore's small land space, this can even be operated outside of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are urging the Advisory Panel to double up their efforts so that we can bring the timeline earlier.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's suggestion of some form of central flight management system, I had, in a previous Parliamentary Sitting announced that we are currently looking into this concept of a central flight management system, whereby registered UAS will be monitored for their activities and where they are operating.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, this is only useful for UAS operators who are cooperative.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As for UAS operators who are uncooperative, with the intention of performing malicious activities, relying on our existing sensors to pick up these illegal activities will be of the utmost importance.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Do we have reason to believe that the recent intrusion at Changi Airport is done by foreigners, whether through foreign control, because we have noted that in the vandalism case on a Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) train at Bishan depot, the intruders were all foreigners?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It will be too early to prejudge whether these are committed by foreigners or locals, or the profile of the perpetrators.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I would urge Mr Ang Wei Neng to give us some time to complete the investigation before we are able to make the necessary announcements.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We know that enforcement is not the easiest of tasks, but it is a necessary step to ensure there are compliance and smooth operations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Is it possible for the Ministry to conduct active enforcement 24/7, like intercepting the drones at the boundary of the no-fly zone, because it seems like it is a very tedious task?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Picking up the activities of drones can be very challenging because the drones are basically quite small in size.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, the ideal situation will be to be able to detect the activities of drones on a 24/7 basis.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But having said that, I think we need to look at the modus operandi of these drone users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have mentioned before, there are cooperative UAS users and, in those cases, the central flight management system will be very useful in identifying exactly where these drone users are operating and the activities of these drones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Should there be situations where there are accidental intrusions into some of these restricted areas, the central flight management system will be able to quickly identify these users and inform them about the accidental intrusions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, we are now dealing with illegal, unauthorised malicious, deliberate activities by UAS users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In these cases, we need to have a risk-stratified approach where certain areas will be given priority in terms of assessing the activities and detecting where they are operating.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: One example will be near aerodromes, such as the Changi Airport area, where we will have the capability to detect as well as disrupt these activities in the shortest possible time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, why were the existing geofencing solutions inadequate to prevent the disruptions in June?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would also like to ask the Senior Minister of State, in light of Minister Ng Eng Hen's comments last week, does CAAS or the Changi Airport Group (CAG) intend to set up a specialist anti-drone unit to deal with drones?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, the Member is correct to say that there are certain solutions like geofencing technology to disallow the operation of certain drones into restricted areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, this will only be possible if the user is using a drone that is fitted with that kind of capability.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, if the users were to use DJI drones, these will be equipped with geofencing capability where the drones will not be allowed to operate in certain restricted areas.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Earlier in January this year, a number of Members asked the same question as a result of what happened at Gatwick.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Senior Minister of State replied to say that we have counter measures to deal with safety and security threats posed by unmanned aerial vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, looking at what has happened, it seems that such countermeasures are inadequate.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, may I ask the Senior Minister of State, what other measures would MOT take to ensure that your measures are adequate to prevent a recurrence?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The second question I have for MOT is whether MOT has quantified the losses caused by the diversion of flights and the closure of the runway and, in light of the massive inconvenience caused to travellers, whether the current maximum fine imposed is adequate.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am trying to say that we should set a stiff punishment to the perpetrators of these offences to make sure that everyone gets the signal that if you disrupt flights, if you cause runways to be closed, the punishment is stiff enough to make sure that everyone reconsiders what they are doing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, when I gave the reply in January this year, we did have the capability to detect and disrupt errant drone users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have also taken a very coordinated approach in managing the current incident.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, after the incidents in Gatwick Airport, we have worked out the standard operating procedure and conducted table-top exercises to run through the operational plans so that we would be able to cope with similar incidents within our own airspace.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I would want to thank all the agencies that had been working day in and day out 24/7 to manage the incidents that had happened at Changi Airport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As a result, we have been able to keep it under control.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have managed to keep disruption to the runway and airport operations to the minimum.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I would also want to take this opportunity to remind all drone users that it is a very, very serious offence to operate unauthorised drones within five km of the airports or military bases, or at altitudes above 200 feet.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Any errant operators of drones will not only pose a danger to aviation, but also to the personal safety of others.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: What are the strategies that we have put in place to prevent similar occurrences?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, CAAS has also been judiciously managing the air traffic operations in Changi to ensure minimal disruptions to the flight operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This can be done through risk-based approaches, in terms of planning for departures and arrivals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These are some measures we are looking at.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I have replied to Mr Dennis Tan's questions, in addition to working with the other agencies, CAAS and CAG are also beefing up their own internal capabilities so that we will be able to manage these incidents more effectively.
